The *Amodaphaliyattheraapadāna* ("Apadāna of the Elder Amodaphaliya") is a short biographical or autobiographical verse narrative in the *Therāpadāna*, a late canonical collection included in the Khuddaka Nikāya of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text records the past merits and former karma of the elder Amodaphaliya, typically centering on the auspicious offering of an *āmoda* fruit in a former life. While no English title is assigned to it on SuttaCentral, the platform records five translations of the poem across five modern languages [SuttaCentral].

No direct external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are listed on SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus finds no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon and its exegetical literature, however, DharmaNexus detects widespread internal text reuse across 43 different texts, totaling 116 matching passages [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial overlap occurs with the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, 18 matches, notably sharing segments §1.1–2.4 with commentary segments §754–757) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the work exhibits extensive stock formulaic and structural parallels with other fruit-offering narratives in the *Therāpadāna*, sharing long identical or near-identical passages (§0.1–7.1 and §2.1–6.1) with poems such as the *Pādaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 507), *Kapitthaphaladāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 514), and *Avaṭaphaliyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 506 and 468) [DharmaNexus].
